title: Facebook Marketplace
seoTitle: Design a Local Marketplace Like Facebook Marketplace
description: Design a peer-to-peer marketplace — creating listings with photos, searching nearby listings with filters, messaging sellers, and marking items sold.
author: Editorial Team

blocks.title: What is Facebook Marketplace?
blocks.text: Facebook Marketplace lets people list items for sale — a used bike, a sofa — and lets buyers nearby browse, search, and message sellers to arrange a deal.

items: Sellers should be able to create a listing with title, description, price, category, location and photos.
Buyers should be able to browse and search listings near them, with filters (category, price range, distance).
Buyers should be able to message a seller about a listing.
Sellers should be able to mark a listing as sold or delete it.

blocks.question: What are the non-functional requirements for this system?

items: New listings searchable within a minute; sold items disappear quickly.
Highly available browsing; eventual consistency is acceptable.
Scale to hundreds of millions of listings and 100M+ daily browsers.
**Listing**: seller, title, description, price, category, location, status, photo references.
**Photo**: image objects in blob storage with resized variants.
**Conversation / Message**: buyer ↔ seller messages tied to a listing.

blocks.code:
POST  /listings { title, description, price, category, lat, lng, photoIds[] } -> Listing
GET   /listings/search?q&category&minPrice&maxPrice&lat&lng&radiusKm&cursor -> Listing[]
PATCH /listings/:id { status: "SOLD" }
POST  /listings/:id/conversations { message } -> Conversation

blocks.text: Photos upload directly to blob storage via presigned URLs; a worker creates thumbnails. The **Listing Service** writes the listing to the primary database and emits a change event.

A **search index** (Elasticsearch/OpenSearch) holds listings with a `geo_point`, category, price and text fields. A single query combines a distance filter, category and price filters, full-text match, and ranking by recency and distance.
Messaging reuses a chat system (see [WhatsApp](/learn/system-design/problem-breakdowns/whatsapp)); each conversation is linked to a listing ID so sellers can see who's interested in what.
The status change writes to the database and propagates to the index, which filters out non-active listings.
1) How do we make location + filter search fast?

approach.text: `SELECT ... WHERE category = ? AND price BETWEEN ? AND ?` and compute distance for every row.

challenges.text: Full scans over hundreds of millions of rows; no relevance ranking.

approach.text: Use PostGIS or a geohash index so the database can find listings within a radius.

challenges.text: Combining geo, text search, filters and ranking at high QPS stresses the primary database.

blocks.title: Dedicated search index fed by CDC

approach.text: Index listings into a search engine with geo, text and filter fields, partitioned by region so queries only touch nearby shards. Keep it in sync with change data capture from the database. Cache popular browse queries (e.g. "Furniture near Austin", first page) for a short TTL.

challenges.text: Eventual consistency between DB and index; a listing may take seconds to appear or disappear.

blocks.text: 2) How do we keep sold items out of results?

Index updates for status changes are prioritised, and the search service double-checks status for the page of results it returns (a cheap batch lookup in a cache), filtering anything marked sold since indexing. This avoids buyers messaging about items that are already gone.

quiz.question: What's the best way to support 'bikes under $200 within 10 km'?
options: SQL distance math on every row
A search index with geo, text and filter fields
quiz.explanation: Search engines combine geo filters, filters and text ranking efficiently.

quiz.question: How does the search index stay in sync with the database?
quiz.explanation: CDC streams every change into the index.

quiz.question: How can you avoid showing just-sold items?
options: Prioritise status updates and recheck status for returned results
quiz.explanation: A cheap status recheck covers indexing lag.

quiz.question: Where should listing photos be stored?
quiz.explanation: Large binary files belong in object storage.
